note: Newest first. Each version's entry is added when main gives the app that version: what is under next, or else the commits that changed the app (docs/RELEASING.md).

entries.title: Hide a sheet's comments, and Night on the board
items: A design sheet's comments can be hidden on the board, to see the design without the pins: press the eye beside Comments, or Shift+C. It stays that way on every sheet until you show them again. The comments are still in the pane, and the one you are writing or have open still shows.
The design sheet's bar has the switch between Day and Night, so you can change it without leaving the board. Your frames stay in your brand's colours.

entries.title: Big design sheets, for your model
items: When several model agents designed on one sheet at once, a frame could come back drawn as another agent's frame, though the right one was saved. Each drawing now has a page of its own, and knitted checks it drew the frame it was asked for. The picture says which frame it is, and at which version of the sheet.
Your model's whole view of a big sheet no longer times out. It is drawn from the pictures the board already keeps of each frame, in one piece, so no seam can show where pieces meet.

Results are much smaller on a big sheet. Reading one frame gives just that frame. Reading a sheet of hundreds of frames comes a page at a time, or one section at a time. Arranging a sheet says what it made, what it removed and which sections changed, not the whole sheet again. Each frame comes with a hash of its code, so a copy can be checked without reading it.

Your model can add or change up to 50 frames in one go, with nothing drawn until it looks at the section. It can ask for a frame's picture small, or not at all, and a new name or note alone comes back in words.
Your model can copy a section, with all its frames, from one of a project's sheets to another, to merge sheets or move a section between them.
A model's tools are listed when it connects. If knitted is updated while a model stays connected, knitted now tells the model to ask you to reconnect it (in Claude Code, /mcp, then Reconnect).

entries.title: Instagram sign-in, explained
items: If your Meta app is set up as a desktop app, Meta turns knitted's Instagram sign-in away. knitted now says so in its own words, with the setting to change: App settings, Advanced, Security, "Native or desktop app?", set to No.

The Instagram steps in the guide now cover what Meta needs before the sign-in can list your account: the account has to be in the business portfolio you pick, and you sign in to Facebook as the person who manages it. knitted does not use an ad account, so there is no need to let Meta create one.

entries.title: A pattern's words and sizes, on a design sheet
items: Pick a pattern on a design sheet, and its pane lists the words you can fill. Change one and leave the field, and it is saved into the pattern itself: the editor, its knits and every sheet show it. Undo on the message takes it back. Words the brand locked are not on offer.

Size on the sheet shows a pattern at another of the sizes it knits at, such as a Story beside the Post, laid out the way a knit at that size would be. The pattern keeps its own size, and Knit starts at the one the sheet shows.
A comment pinned on a pattern shown at another size tells your model the stitch under the pin at that size. Your model can set the size too, with arrange_design and set_design_frame.
A part's pane on the sheet lists its slots.

entries.title: Instagram through Meta's Unified login
items: Meta no longer gives new apps an Instagram app ID, and Instagram's own sign-in turns their App ID away as an invalid platform app. Instagram in Settings, Social now takes your Meta app's App ID and App secret with a Configuration ID from its API setup with Unified login, and Connect signs you in on Facebook with that configuration.
Pick your business and your Instagram accounts as you sign in: each one you pick is connected. The sign-in is your business's, so it does not run out.
Posts, Stories, Reels, carousels and their numbers work as before, through Facebook's Graph. An older app with an Instagram app ID keeps Instagram's own sign-in: leave the Configuration ID empty.
The guide's Instagram steps are rewritten for Unified login, with the older app's steps after them.

entries.title: Patterns, Yarn and parts on a design sheet
items: The + beside a section's name adds a pattern, a picture or video from Yarn, or a part, beside the pages: a campaign's posts beside the page they go with. Pick one by its picture, or find it by name. It starts at its own size, in its own shape.

It is the thing itself, not a copy. A pattern or a part is drawn by the editor's own renderer, in your brand, so a change to it in the editor, by your model or anywhere else shows on the sheet. A deleted one leaves a note in its place.

Picked, it has a tab of its own: Open in the editor, Knit and Ask your model for a pattern; Open in Yarn for a picture; Open in the editor or in Parts for a part. Take it off the sheet leaves the thing where it is. A sheet's card counts them apart from its frames: 4 sections, 10 frames, 2 pieces.

Pin a comment on a pattern as on a frame: your model is told which stitch is under the pin, and changes the pattern itself. Your model can add pieces too, with arrange_design, and view_design draws them with the rest.

entries.title: Comments on a design sheet, as on a knit
items: The pane beside a design sheet has a knit's tabs: Frame, for the frame you picked, with its name, size and code, and Comments, with how many are open.
With a frame picked, its comments come first, and all of the sheet's are a press away. Ask your model to do all of them does the ones shown.
A pin pressed picks its frame and opens its comment.
Under the frame you pick: Zoom to it, Pin a comment, and Ask your model, which starts a chat about that frame alone.

entries.title: Move sections and frames about the sheet
items: Drag a section by its name to anywhere on the board: it lands on the 40 pixel grid, and the sections you have not placed stay where they stood, so nothing else moves. With its name picked, the arrow keys move it 40 pixels, and 200 with Shift.
Drag a section's right edge in to wrap its frames into rows, and out to have them in one row again. With the edge picked, the left and right arrow keys do the same.

Sections never cover one another. One that grows, by wrapping or by more frames, pushes those under it down; a section put down over another stays where you put it, and the other moves under it. While you drag, nothing else moves.
Drag a frame to another place in its section, or into another section: a bar shows where it will go.
The board has a dot grid, which spreads out as you zoom out so it never crowds.
Tidy up puts every section back in one column, in their order, and Undo puts them back where they were.

Zooming keeps up. A pinch, or Ctrl with the wheel, is drawn at once about the pointer, and which frames are live or pictures is picked once it stops. The zoom buttons, the keys and a double-click glide there; with reduced motion on, they go straight there.
The zoom menu has Whole sheet, to see all of it, beside Fit the width. A double-click on a section's name zooms to that section, and the zoom buttons and keys go out to 2%, as a pinch did.
On a sheet bigger than the window, a map in the bottom left corner shows its sections and where you are; a press or a drag on it goes there.
A section or frame you add is brought into view when it is out of it. Dragging something at the fit keeps the zoom as it is, so the board does not zoom as it grows.

Settings, Social says where to find each Meta ID: the Instagram app ID is on the Instagram use case's API setup page, not the App ID in App settings, which Instagram turns away as an invalid platform app. The guide says so too.

entries.title: Design sheets without a limit
items: A design sheet takes as many frames and sections as the site needs. The limits of 200 frames and 40 sections are gone.

The board loads only what you are looking at. A sheet opens without its code: a frame small on screen is a picture of it, drawn once and kept until the frame changes; a frame big enough to read is drawn live; frames out of view are outlines. A sheet of 101 frames opened in 174 milliseconds instead of 643, in 11 MB of memory instead of 70.
The studio measures each frame once and keeps its height, so the board is laid out as it will be before you scroll to a frame, and nothing moves as frames come in.

Sections can stand anywhere on the board, on a 40 pixel grid, with a width their frames wrap to in rows. Your model places them with arrange_design for now; sections not placed stand in a column under the placed ones.
Undo keeps a frame's code once, not once for every step. On one sheet, a history of 50 steps went from 59 MB to 1.3 MB; history already kept is converted when the studio opens.
Zoom goes out to 2%, from 5%. Far out, a section's name shrinks with the board once it would no longer fit above the section.

entries.title: Check the claims
items: The editor checks what a pattern's words say about the business against its Brief. With nothing selected, Claims, under Before it knits, has your model read each claim beside the Brief: what the business does, works with or costs, numbers, names and quotes.

Each claim gets one of four answers. Backed: the Brief says it. Against: the Brief says otherwise. Not available yet: the Brief says planned, in beta or by invitation, and the words say it as if anyone can have it now. Not in the Brief: nothing backs it, which may be a gap in the Brief.

Where the Brief says it differently, the card shows what it says and a true way to say it. Use this wording puts that in the quote's place, as one change you can undo, and Show it picks the text the claim is in.
Change the words and the check says it is out of date, with Check again. Going to another page and back keeps the check, without asking your model again.

Without a key, Claims says how to check them: add a key, or connect Claude Code, which can now check_claims. That tool gives the words and the Brief side by side, and costs nothing more. The copywriting guide asks for it before words are knitted.
Checks are counted in Spending, as Claims checks.

A video with footage at more than one rate is knitted at the rate of most of it, by time on screen and the part of the frame it fills. A full-frame clip shot at 25 with a small one at 30 in a corner was knitted at 30 before, and every pan in it hitched. The warning for footage that still steps now says which rate the video chose and why.

entries.title: Knitting as it happens, and video posters
items: A video's card shows its poster: the moment its pattern shows whole, a frame of the video itself, with how long it runs. Before, every video card showed its first frame, which is often empty.
Point at a video's card and it plays there, muted, with a line for where it is. Moving away puts the poster back. Where your system asks for less motion, it stays still.
The knit view's player, its versions, Posts and the Post dialog show the poster too, and a folder of videos peeks with them.
Videos knitted before this get their poster the first time they are shown, made from the video and then kept.
While a knit runs, the queue shows the file being drawn as soon as its frames start, and every file of the knit in its shape: done ones as they land, the rest as outlines.

entries.title: Past chats without a key, and a Download page that is never behind
items: A chat had with your model stays there to read when no key is set. In place of the box to write in, it says how to write in it again: add your Anthropic key, or connect Claude Code.
A new chat with no key still says what you could ask and the two ways in.

The Download page shows a new version, or a Mac's disk image, the moment it is up. It reads the release folder in your browser, so it no longer waits for the site to be built again. With no connection it shows the list it was built with.

entries.title: The Brief, Swatch and Parts, in one shape with the rest
items: The Brief reads beside an outline of the profile's parts, which marks the part you are reading and goes to one with a press. The website, with Sync again, and your notes for your model sit beside it and stay in sight.
New swatch is one menu of the three ways to start: blank or from a template, from a website, or from a file.
Each swatch has its own menu, from its ... button or a right-click: Use for this project, Duplicate, Move to folder, Export and Delete. M and Delete work on its row too.

Each colour is one row: its well, its own name, its hex, and what it is used as. Colours, Fonts, Logos, Voice and Shape are each a card, with their actions in the head, and Add a logo finds a picture in Yarn by name.
Parts are cards of one height, each part centred and scaled in a well of one shape, with Edit, or Edit a copy for a starter, and a menu for the rest.
The pictures to pick from in Make a photo or video and in Add a logo are squares of one size.

entries.title: The Windows app opens
items: The Windows app opens. As its server started, it read a folder named by the computer that built it, which on Windows is not a folder at all, and the window never came. Reading a PDF on Windows had the same fault, and so did the scheduler that sends posts out at their time.
knitted shows its window as soon as it starts, saying it is starting. If it cannot start, it says so, with a way to open what happened, instead of showing nothing.
Each launch keeps a log beside the library, and the launch before it too. Help, Show the log finds it.
Knits made on Windows are filed under their own name, not the whole path to them.

entries.title: Posts, Insights and Stock, ready to start
items: Posts shows where a post can go now: one chip per network, with the account it posts as, or what is left to set up. Each opens that network in Settings, already open.
With nothing posted, Posts says how to start: Open Knits when an account is connected, or Set up Social when none is, and every knit has Download and Copy caption to post it yourself.
Insights shows what will be there before anything is posted, dimmed, with a way to the project's Posts.
Stock says where finds go under the search, where they come from, and offers searches to start from for photos, videos and sound, each run with a press.
In Ask, a chat's delete shows on the open chat and the one you point at, not on every chat in the list.

entries.title: Settings, one list
items: Settings is one list in four groups, Studio, Your model, Making and Posting, and each line says how that part stands: a key saved, what is spent this month, how many accounts are connected. The address keeps the part you are on, so Back goes to the one before.
Every part is made of cards of rows: what a setting does on the left, its control on the right. A key is asked for the same way everywhere: where it is kept, then Save, Test and Remove in one row.
Social shows the six networks as rows, each saying what it posts and how it stands. One opens at a time, as three steps: register the redirect, give knitted your app, and connect an account.
A main button that cannot be pressed yet is grey and flat, not a faded orange. Every page sits on the same edge, and Projects is headed Projects.
Settings, Generate is now Settings, Photos and video, in the studio, your model's tools and the docs.

entries.title: Knit, ask and make, said before you press
items: Knit lists each file it will make, one row each with its shape, its size in pixels and its checks, and says what each comes back as: new, the next version of its knit, another format of one, or the same as the one there, which is kept rather than drawn again. Show me picks the stitch a check is about.
The sizes to knit are shown as their shapes, and the button leaves out the files that are there already as they are. With nothing changed it says so, and turning off Reuse draws them again.

Ask your model shows what it is about, with its picture, and says what comes back before you ask: for a knit, its next version, with this one kept under Versions; for a pattern, changes you can take back in its History. ⌘↵ asks.

Make a photo or video puts the price beside the choices that change it: the total, each one, and what the other qualities cost. The month's spending is in the footer, and the button says what it makes and for how much.
Pictures to work from can be added from Yarn in the window itself, found by name.

entries.title: Keys, sorting, sizes and parts
items: ? shows every keyboard shortcut, anywhere in the studio, grouped and searchable, with this computer's keys: ⌘ on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere. In the editor ⌘/ opens it too, and the editor's buttons show the same keys.

In Knits, Yarn and Patterns, keys act on the one in focus or on the ones picked: M moves to a folder and Delete asks first, in all three; T adds a tag in Knits and Yarn, F makes a favourite in Knits, and R renames in Patterns and Yarn. Each menu shows the key beside what it does.
Sort says which way it runs, like Name, A to Z or Last changed, newest first, and Reverse the order turns it round. Both are kept for next time.

Custom size in the editor takes any width and height, keeps the shape when asked, starts from sizes that are used, like a link preview or a YouTube thumbnail, and draws the new size over the old one before you make it.
Save as part shows the part as it will look, starts its kind from what is picked, and asks who decides each slot: each pattern, or the brand, the same in every pattern.

entries.title: Dialogs and menus, one shape everywhere
items: Every dialog has one shape: what it does as its title, where it lands under that, a body that scrolls on its own, and its buttons in a footer that stays put.

New project asks for the website first and reads it as the project fills in, with the swatch, the profile and the page pictures each to tick. The starter pack and Blank are cards, each showing what it makes.
New pattern shows each size as its shape, with where it goes: Stories, Reels, TikTok and Shorts; Instagram and LinkedIn feeds; YouTube, X and websites. Custom asks for the width and height in place.
New folder shows the folders it makes as you type, the new ones lit. A name that is taken says so, with a way to the one there.
Move is a tree you can search, with what each folder holds and where things are now. A folder made in it goes in the one lit and is picked.
Tag works on many at once. A tag all of them have comes off with its x, one some have goes on the rest with its +, and the project's own tags are offered first, the most used at the top.

A knit has a menu of its own, from its ... button or a right-click: open, post, copy the caption, ask your model, move, tag, favourite, download and delete. A Yarn file has one too, with cutting out a part and making a photo or video from it. With several picked, the menu acts on all of them and says so.
Every menu has the same order. A folder's menu makes a folder in it, and in Knits downloads it as a zip. Deleting a folder says nothing in it goes; deleting a project shows what it holds.
Esc that closes a menu or a dialog closes only that: what is picked stays picked.

entries.title: One card per knit, with its versions and formats
items: Knits shows each knit once. Ask your model for a change, or knit a pattern again after changing it, and the new one takes the old one's place, in the same folder, with its caption, tags and star. The old one is kept under the knit's Versions, to look at, bring back or delete.
The same picture as a JPEG, at 2x or at 60 frames a second is a format of one knit, not another card. A knit's Formats tab lists its files, downloads any of them, and knits another one.
Knits made before this version are sorted into versions and formats once, the first time the studio opens. Nothing is deleted.
Opening a knit shows it large, with its post, versions, formats, comments and details in tabs beside it. Step to the knit before or after with the arrows, or with ← and →.
Every version, in the Knits filters, lists every file again, each saying which version it is.

A knit's caption shows how it fits each network as you write, hashtags included. Make it shorter, longer, more playful or for LinkedIn in one press, or say what to change. Captions written over are kept under Earlier captions, to use again.
Post shows what is going and where, and checks the caption against each network you pick. With nothing connected yet, it shows where to connect, and how to post it yourself.
A file renamed with a slash in its name, like Slide 1/5, keeps its whole name.

entries.title: Captions you can make longer
items: Asking your model for a longer caption, like one for LinkedIn that tells the whole story, works now. The model thinks before it writes, and that thinking used up the room the caption needed, so a longer one was cut off part way and came back as "could not be read".
Captions come back in the shape knitted asks for, so they always read. A caption with line breaks between paragraphs keeps them.
Say which network a caption is for, and your model keeps it within what that network takes: 280 characters on X, 500 on Threads, 3,000 on LinkedIn.
If an answer is ever cut off, it says so, and what to do.

entries.title: The editor and Ask, finished from the design sheets
items: The editor's pattern list shows each pattern drawn small beside its name, so the one you want is easy to find.

With nothing selected, the inspector runs the checks Knit runs and says what to fix before it knits: missing files, low contrast, text that will not fit. Pick a problem to select what it is about. It checks again after each save.
Ask shows what your model is doing in plain words, like Filling headline on Spring sale, and says Filled once it is done.
While your model knits, its step shows which file it is on, with a bar that fills as it goes.
A note your model has finished writing shows once, in What it did, not twice.

entries.title: Tidier screens, from the design sheets
items: Yarn has one Add button for every other way in: make a photo or a video, free stock, from a link, or save text. Upload stays the button to press.
Tags in Yarn and Knits are behind one Tags button, so the filters fit on one line. The tag picked shows beside it.
Folder tiles in Yarn and Knits show a peek of up to three pictures from inside.
With nothing selected, the editor lists the pattern's slots, free ones first, with what each holds. Pick one to select it on the canvas.

A chat started from an Ask your model button is named for what you asked, not for what the studio told your model about the page. Chats named that way before are named again once, unless you changed the name.
Chats are grouped by day: today, yesterday, this week and before.
Without a key, Ask shows what you could ask, and links to adding a key or connecting Claude Code.
A swatch's buttons fit on one row, with Delete apart at the end.

entries.title: A studio that arrives in place
items: While a section loads, it shows its filters, folders and cards at their real sizes, so nothing jumps when they arrive. The project's name keeps its height too.
Cards and folders fade in as they arrive, a moment apart, and stay put after. With reduced motion on, they only fade.
Going to another page, a thin orange line across the top shows it is on its way. A fast page shows nothing.
Notes in the corner have a close button and at most three show at once. When something goes wrong the note is red and stays longer.
A button that started something spins where its icon was until it is done.
Folder tiles are all one height, with what is inside on one line, and the whole name when you point at it.
A design sheet opened from its address shows a header, a footer and any other frame that fits what is in it at its real height straight away, not at a guess until something changes.
A knit that has just arrived shows its whole selection ring and your model's red outline, not cut off at its edges.

entries.title: Follow your model as it sorts folders
items: Following your model while it files things or renames a folder, the studio opens that folder, and outlines it in red with what your model is doing.
Each Pattern, Yarn file, Part or knit it moves is outlined too, where it goes. Knits are outlined like everything else now.
A design frame that shows a picture from the Brief's reference, like a page of your site as it is today, now shows it when your model looks at the frame, not a grey placeholder.
Making photos, the note that they are in Yarn shows once, even on a busy computer.

entries.title: Comments your model can act on, pinned to the spot
items: Open a knit and press Add a comment, then click the spot that should change and say what. In a video the comment is at the moment you chose, and its pin shows round then.
On a design sheet, Comments on the bar opens the comments, and a click on a frame pins one there. Pins stay on the board at any zoom, and press one to open it.
Each comment is numbered with its pin. Reply, resolve, open again or delete it. A knit's card and a sheet's card show how many comments are open.

Ask your model to do this, on a comment, or Ask your model to do all: your model sees the spot with the pin on it and a close-up, is told which stitch or which element of the HTML is under it, makes the change, and answers each comment, resolving it when it is done.
For models: list_comments, view_comment and reply_comment.
A link written on a button, such as the whole knit, is drawn as a link, not a grey button. The Brief's Look at it in the Swatch tab is fixed the same way.

entries.title: Download one section with everything in it
items: A section's menu on a design sheet downloads everything in that section: a ZIP with the section as a picture, its frames as HTML and CSS, the fonts and pictures they use, tokens.css and tokens.json, and a style guide of just what that section is drawn with.
A section's menu downloads its code on its own too, beside the picture it already had.

entries.title: Download a design with everything, and a style guide
items: A design sheet's Download menu has Everything: a ZIP with the sheet and each section as pictures, every frame as HTML and CSS, the fonts and pictures it uses, tokens.css and tokens.json, and a style guide.

The style guide, as a page and as a picture, shows what the design is drawn with: the brand's colours, fonts and corners with the CSS variable for each and where it is used, every type size and weight, the spacing, the shadows, and any colour written in the code that is not the brand's.
The list of design sheets can download everything from each sheet's menu too.

entries.title: Pick the model as you talk to it, or let Auto pick
items: Beside every message box and in every Ask your model window, a Model menu says which model answers. Pick another at any time; a task that is running takes it from its next step. It is the same choice as Settings, Model.

Auto picks the model for each task, so it costs no more than it needs: Claude Haiku 5.5 for a quick change, Claude Opus 5.5 for layout, design sheets, drawing and motion, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 for the rest.

Part way through, Auto moves up a model when steps keep failing or a task turns out bigger, keeping what the model worked out so far. It never moves down part way, and on a long chat it was just in, it stays where reading the chat again would cost more.
Each answer says which model gave it, and in Auto, why, and when it moved up. Auto is what a new setup starts on.

entries.title: See your model at work everywhere, and know when it is done
items: Wherever your model works, that thing is outlined in red with its name and what it is doing: a Pattern, Yarn, Part, Swatch or design sheet in its list, a batch in the knitting queue, and the project tab it is under, as well as each Stitch in the editor.
On a design sheet, the frame your model is designing or looking at is outlined on the board too, and the panel in the corner says what it is doing. Follow brings each frame it works on into view.

When a run you started ends, the studio tells you on whatever page you are on, with the first line of its answer and Open the chat. Behind another window, your computer shows a notification. Turn either off in Settings, Model.

On a design sheet, picking a second frame with the first one open showed the first frame's code for the second, and saving would have written it there. Each frame now keeps its own unsaved changes, and has them again when you go back to it.

entries.title: A whole design sheet downloads as a picture again
items: A design sheet too big for one browser window, like a whole site of a hundred frames, downloaded as a blank picture of a few kilobytes. It is now drawn in tiles and put together, so every frame is in the picture.
Your model, looking at a whole sheet, had the same blank picture, and now sees every frame too.

entries.title: Zoom and drag anywhere, favourites, and knits by type
items: In the editor and on a design sheet, hold Space or turn on the Hand (H) to drag from anywhere, even over a stitch or a frame. The middle button drags too.
A zoom menu in both: fit to screen, zoom to selection, 50%, 100% and 200%, with keys for each (Shift+1, Shift+2, Shift+0, and + and -).
A design sheet now zooms to 400%, and a pinch or Ctrl and scroll zooms about the pointer. Double-click a frame to zoom to it, and the space round it to fit again.
Star the knits you like, one at a time or several together, and show only your favourites. Your model can list them too.
Knits narrow to pictures or videos, and to a size: Story (Stories, Reels, TikTok, Shorts), Post, Square, Landscape or Banner.

entries.title: Footage at its own frame rate, and fewer false alarms
items: A video whose footage was all shot at 24 or 25 frames a second, as most stock footage is, is now made at that rate, so no frame of it shows twice. At 30, one frame in six did, and every pan hitched.
Footage at mixed rates, like 25 beside 30, is warned about, with which clip hitches.
The voiceover check no longer calls macOS or iPhone code, and lets the voice say the plain words of a comment or a result shown beside a command.

entries.title: Design sheets: a whole site on one board, in labelled sections
items: Designs, a new tab in every project: a site's colours and type, the pieces its pages share, and each page on a computer and a phone, on one board in labelled sections, like a Figma file.
Start one from your brand, with Foundations, Components and a home page drawn with your Swatch, or blank. Every colour, font and corner follows the Swatch, so a change there changes the whole design.
Select a frame to change its name, size and code, and see it on the board as you type. Undo walks back through your changes and your model's.
Design with your model: it designs each page, sees what it made, and fixes it, while you watch the board change.
Download the sheet, a section or a frame as a picture, or the whole design as HTML and CSS, with your brand's tokens and fonts, for whoever builds the site.

entries.title: Make photos and video with your own key, priced before you make them
items: Make, on a project's Yarn page: say what to make, choose its shape, how many and the quality, and see what it will cost before you make it. It lands in Yarn while you carry on.
Add an OpenAI or Google Gemini key in Settings, Generate. OpenAI makes photos; Google makes photos and video, with sound.
Make a photo from this, on any picture in Yarn: a new photo from your product or your mascot, or a short video that starts from it.
Each file says who made it, from what, what you asked for and what it cost, and counts toward your limits in Settings, Spending.
Your model can make them too, with generate_image and generate_video, and asks the price first.

entries.title: Your model draws: icon sets, mascot poses and badges, as SVG
items: Draw with your model, on a project's Yarn page: say what to draw, such as icons for your website or your mascot waving, and your model draws it as SVG and keeps it in Yarn. SVG stays sharp at any size.
To draw from your mascot or your logo, upload it and name it in what you ask. Ask your model, on a picture, now suggests drawing it in new poses.

Your model sees each drawing on white, on dark and at icon sizes before you do, and puts a set side by side to check it belongs together. It draws one again in place, so every Pattern that uses it updates, and never draws over a file you uploaded.
A drawing is marked Drawn by your model, with what you asked for and what it was drawn from.
SVG thumbnails are sharp: an icon was drawn at its own small size and blown up.
The activity panel says what your model is doing when it searches and adds free stock.

entries.title: Free stock photos, video, music and sound, with their credits
items: Stock, in the side bar: search free photos, videos, music and sound effects and add them to a project's Yarn or to the Library. Free stock on a project's Yarn page, and Find free stock in the editor's Yarn panel, open it for that project.

Openverse works with no key: openly licensed photos and sound from across the web. Add a free Pixabay key in Settings, Stock, for its photos and video. A Pexels key you already have works too. A key is kept in your computer's secret store and only sent to its own site.
Only what a business may use freely is shown: CC0, the public domain, CC BY, and Pixabay's and Pexels' own licences.
A file you add keeps its credit and licence. Open it in Yarn to see whether it needs a credit, copy the credit line, and open its page.
Your model can search with search_stock and add the few you will use with add_stock.

entries.title: Changing Parts in the editor, and the Library, now in the app
items: 0.1.19 never reached anyone: the app failed to build its Library page. This version has everything listed under 0.1.19, below, and the Library page opens.

entries.title: Change a Part in the editor, and a Library every project shares
items: Edit, on a Part of your own, opens it in the editor: the canvas is the Part, and every change is saved to it as you go, one new version for the sitting. Every Pattern that uses it shows the change at once, and Accept the update takes its new shape there too. Done goes back to Parts.

In a Pattern, select a Part and choose Change the part to open it. A Part written in code opens as its markup and CSS. The starter Parts stay as they come: Edit a copy makes one of your own and opens it.
Lock a slot in a Part and it is locked in every Pattern that uses the Part straight away, before anyone accepts the update.

The Library, in the side bar: files every project shares, like a logo, a font or a photo you use for every brand. They are in every project's Yarn in the editor, under From the Library. Move to the Library, on a file in a project, puts one there, and every Pattern that uses it keeps it. Move into a project takes one back when no other project uses it.
Your model changes a Part with edit_part, adds files to the Library with library: true, and moves one in or out with share_yarn. list_yarn marks the Library's files.

entries.title: How your posts did, what works, and posts that go out with the window closed
items: Each post that went out shows its numbers in Posts: views, likes, comments, shares and saves, and how many of those who saw it did something. knitted asks an hour after it goes out, then after 6 hours, a day, 3 days, a week, 2 weeks and a month; Check now asks straight away.

Insights, in the side bar: each platform's views, every post against the usual for its own account about a week in, and what did better, in a sentence, such as which got more views, videos or pictures, mornings or evenings, short captions or long. Something is said only when each side has 3 posts or more.
Your model reads the same with post_insights, and list_posts now gives each post's numbers.

Instagram, Threads, TikTok and YouTube are asked with the sign-in you already gave. X charges for each look, so it is off until you turn on Ask X for numbers too, in Settings, Social. LinkedIn gives no numbers to apps like this one, and says so on the post.

Close the window while posts are waiting and knitted stays in the menu bar (the system tray on Windows and Linux) until the last one is out, then quits. Quitting with posts waiting asks first. Turn it off in Settings, Social.

The site's feature list said ten things were coming that have been here for a while: the Pattern editor, Fill mode, batch knitting, Yarn, Parts, Motion, voiceover, your model in the studio, Projects and the installers. It now says what is there, with posting and Insights added.

entries.title: Scenes that change, sound you can hear and move, footage that knits fast
items: Seven ways out: Fade out, Slide out up, down, left and right, Shrink away and Wipe away. The Inspector's Animate section groups the animations into Come in, Go out and Keep moving.

Change scene, on the timeline: at the playhead, what is on screen goes out, a little apart, and what comes next comes in from then, headline first. Before, scenes were only covered by the next one, with their words still underneath.
Select several things and animate them together: they start a little apart, top to bottom, and one Undo takes back the lot.

Checks for words still on screen when the next scene comes in over them, for a part that shows before the box it sits in (a terminal's dots before the window, a button's words after the button sat empty), and for a part left behind when its box goes. Text that something comes in over now counts as gone for reading time.
Footage plays from the start of its file when it comes in, so a clip in a second scene no longer begins part way through. Starts from, in the Inspector, starts it later.

Footage knits several times faster: each clip is copied once at the size it is drawn, and frames are saved with a faster setting that keeps every pixel. In a test with 4K footage, a frame took about 200 ms instead of 600, and every video knits faster.
Hear the voice and music while the timeline plays, with a button to turn it off.
Move a sound, start it later in its file, change its loudness and loop music, from the Voice panel. Music can start at its chorus instead of its quiet opening.
Fit to clips counts the sounds too, so a voiceover is not cut off where the last animation ends.
Your model changes scene with change_scene, and its guide covers exits, scenes, what sits in a box, and where music starts.
Seven pages of the guide said things were not built that are: Yarn, Patterns and the editor, Fill mode, Batch knitting, Motion, Voiceover and Using your model now describe what is there.

entries.title: Post to your own accounts, now or at a time
items: Post a knit to Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Threads, X and YouTube: open it and press Post, or pick several and press Post together for a carousel. Post it now, at a time, or keep it as a draft.

Each platform's limits are checked as you write, before anything is scheduled: X's 280 characters, with a link counting as 23; TikTok taking videos only; the shapes Instagram takes; YouTube's title. A caption too long for one platform gets a field of its own.
A project's new Posts tab shows what went out, with a link to each, what is scheduled, and what needs you. Post a draft now, move a time, or cancel.

Connect your accounts in Settings, Social, through a developer app of your own on each platform. There is no knitted server in between, so your sign-ins stay in your computer's secret store. The new guide, Posting to social accounts, walks through each platform.

Posts go out while knitted is open. One due while it was closed goes out when it opens, if that is within two hours, and otherwise waits as missed for you to post or move. YouTube publishes a scheduled video itself, knitted open or not.

A post that fails before anything was sent, because the network dropped or the platform was busy, is tried again twice. One that fails after says to look on the platform first, so nothing is posted twice.

Instagram and Threads fetch what they post from a public address, so knitted puts each file in a bucket of yours (R2, S3, B2, Spaces, MinIO) or a FileFreak folder just before posting, and removes it after. Test in Settings checks that it works.
TikTok posts follow TikTok's rules for apps: you pick who sees each one, with nothing picked for you, and comments, duets and stitches stay off until you turn them on.
Your model can post too, with schedule_post. What it makes are drafts for you to schedule, unless you let it schedule in Settings, Social.

entries.title: Voices that say it, Briefs that know what is ready
items: A voiceover line can say one thing and caption another. Write the caption after a bar, like Roll it back from the terminal | filefreak sites rollback 3, and the voice says the words, while the screen shows the command. Your model does the same.

The voice no longer reads code aloud without a warning. Check and Knit say when a line reads out a command, a path or a file name, or the command typed on screen, and suggest saying what it does instead.

One take is cut into lines only where the voice really paused, and where each line's length fits its words. Lines it ran together stay one clip, so a word is never split between two, and the voiceover says which lines those are.

Asking your model costs less. It used to check on a voiceover again and again while it was spoken, each time re-reading the whole conversation: 41 of 59 steps in one real ask. Now it waits for the voiceover in one step, and is told to do independent steps at once.

Your model has a copywriting guide: only what the Brief says is true and available now, no invented prices, quotes or reviews, a hook from the reader's own day, and variety across a batch. The posts guide now covers Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, X, Threads and YouTube one by one.

Building the Brief reads your website as a visitor sees it, in the browser, so sections a page draws with JavaScript are read too. notch.fm's Works with band, which says Spotify is planned, used to arrive empty.

The Brief gets today's date and a section for what is available now and what is planned, coming soon or in beta, so nothing planned is written as ready. It suggests as many ideas as the material supports, not always twelve.
Short picture descriptions, like a service's name in a Works with band, are read now; a bare 'logo' still is not.
Music advice is the same everywhere: 0.4 to 0.6 under a voice, since every track is brought to one loudness first.

entries.title: A long list, worked through
items: Keep writing while your model answers: what you send waits its turn under the conversation, and goes when the answer is in. Take any of it out of the queue. If you stop a run, the rest wait for you.

Your model can set how loud the music is under a voiceover. It used to try names for the setting that did nothing; now it is told the name, and a name it gets wrong is refused out loud instead of ignored.
Projects is the first page now, and it and every project's tabs show the knits under way, so you can see what is knitting everywhere at once.
Knits nobody has opened yet say New, and Mark all seen clears them.

Pick several patterns, knits or Yarn files at once: Cmd or Ctrl-click, Shift-click for a run, Cmd or Ctrl+A for everything shown, Escape to clear. Then tag, file, download, duplicate or delete them together.
Ask your model about a pattern, a knit or a file from its own menu: say what to change, and it does it in the chat.
Spending: what your model has cost this month, and a limit that stops it before it goes over.
Copy in Yarn is called Saved text, which says what it is.
Knit at 60 frames a second for fast motion.
Your model reads a guide before it works, topic by topic: patterns, motion, voiceovers, posts and more.
Frames are drawn about three times faster.
Footage in a video no longer stutters. At Story size every third frame used to repeat.
Type-on types a letter at a time, each in its place, and stitch-in brings the words in one by one, each rising into place.

A second animation on the same thing no longer cancels the first, the slow zoom works on video too, and a pulse keeps its beat. Entrances ease in evenly instead of jumping most of the way in the first frames.
Text that slides in is as sharp as a still before and after it moves.
Sound no longer crackles: the finished file's peaks are measured and kept under the limit.
Every voice line and music track is brought to one loudness, music dips once under a voice instead of swelling between words, and music cut off by the end of the video fades out.
Videos come out at the loudness the apps play at, and a knit that does not says so.
Music set too quiet to hear under a voice is flagged, with the level that suits.
Colours in videos match the pattern: a brand red no longer turns orange. Videos also start playing before they have finished loading.
Headlines are balanced over their lines, with no word left alone at the end. Code keeps its indentation, and a pop grows from where the words are.
A short word that starts a sentence stays with the word after it, and a number stays with its unit, so a line no longer ends on a lone "It" or splits "5 GB".
Text that fits its box is no longer reported as cut off: a display font's tall ascent, or a word still rising in, set it off.
Contrast warnings look at what is really behind the words, like a button, a card or a band, instead of the page.
Stories warn when words or a logo sit under the app's top bar or reply bar.
A knit made before its pattern was last changed says so, so an old file is not posted by mistake.
A font knitted does not have, or one that fails to load, is reported instead of quietly drawn in a stand-in.
Website pictures are taken at twice the pixels, so a part cut out of one stays sharp in a post.
Motion checks catch entrances too fast to see, type-on too fast to read, and long stills anywhere in a video, the end included.
Your model can page through every knit in a project, not just the newest 30.

entries.title: Knits under way, in one place
items: Knits under way are one panel instead of a row each: the one knitting, with a bar that fills as its frames are drawn and what it is doing now, and the ones waiting their turn listed under it by name. Cancel any of them, or all at once.

entries.title: See your model at work anywhere
items: While a model works, a card in the corner of every page says what it is doing and what it last wrote, with Show me and Follow. Make it smaller to keep it out of the way.
Follow no longer gets stuck on the page it is leaving: a move that does not land is made again.

Your model can look inside videos now: a sheet of frames from across one, each marked with its time, and a closer look at any part. For audio it gets the length and how the loudness moves. So it can sort and name files whatever they are called.
The chat page no longer scrolls on past the conversation into blank space.
The list of chats can be folded away, for more room to read.

entries.title: Any voice model, used to the full
items: A voice server shows its own voices and models in Settings, including the presets its model has but does not list (Qwen3's Ryan, Serena and the rest). Type any voice name it takes.
Give a style in words ("warm, deep and confident") for models that take one, and any other options your server takes, as JSON.
A voice server's own error now shows in Settings, like an unsupported voice, instead of "Something broke on our side". A model name the server does not have falls back to its own speech model.
A voiceover is spoken in one take, so the voice sounds the same from the first line to the last, then cut at the pauses into a clip per line.
A voiceover's sound now runs to the video's last frame, so a knit no longer refuses it as a few milliseconds short.

entries.title: Captions, hashtags and music for each knit
items: Open a knit and your model writes what goes with the post: a caption in the business's voice, hashtags, and a track from the project's music, with why it fits. It reads the Brief, the post's words and, for a picture, the picture itself.

Write it again as many times as you like, or say what to change first (shorter, more playful, mention Saturday). Edit any of it yourself, pick another track, and copy the caption and hashtags in one go.

entries.title: Sharp pictures
items: Pictures in Yarn and the Brief are sharp in the grid. A tall picture, such as a website page, used to show a small thumbnail stretched; its tile now shows the top of the page.
Choosing a project's picture shows its images as a proper grid of squares, instead of squeezed strips.

entries.title: Videos that play, and room to work
items: A video in a pattern plays now: in the editor, and in the knit. Before, only its first frame showed.
The page no longer scrolls past its end into a blank band.
The editor's top bar keeps its place when a lot is going on: the trail and what your model is doing are cut short, never drawn over each other.
Yarn and Knits show the most used tags, and the rest are in a menu you can search.
With more than one model at work, the side bar shows each one, and you can follow any of them.
A video's thumbnail has a play mark on it.
Knits have tags, to find them by.
The chats are kept apart by project: the Ask page shows one project's chats at a time, and the editor only that project's.

entries.title: A brief for every project
items: A Brief for every project: what your model knows about the business. Sync it with the business's website and knitted reads the public pages, has your model write a profile from them (who they are, what they offer and to whom, how they sound, the facts to get right), and pictures every page on a desktop and a phone. Or write the profile yourself. Your model reads it before it writes, and a change your model makes to it can be undone in the Brief tab.

Give a website when you make a project, and the project starts from it: its swatch read from the site, a profile, and pictures of every page. Sync again at any time to bring all of it up to date: a page pictured before is replaced where it is.

The Brief's reference is a shelf of files to look at and read, like menus, brochures and pictures of the website, kept apart from the Yarn you put in patterns. Move a file between the two with Move to the Brief and Move to Yarn.
PDFs can go in Yarn and the reference. Turn their pages, read their words, and cut a page, or a part of a picture, out as a new picture in Yarn.
Every section can be shown as a grid or a list, sorted and searched: Patterns, Yarn, the reference, Swatch, Parts and Knits. Each remembers its choice on this computer.
One trail at the top of every project page says where you are, from Projects to the folder you are in. Each tab says what it is for, and more buttons say what they do when you point at them.
Your model's replies are formatted, with headings, lists and code, and yours and its are easy to tell apart.
In the editor, the canvas cannot be scrolled or panned out of reach, panning and zooming are gentler, and both side bars fold away (Ctrl or Cmd and \ folds both).

While your model works on a pattern, the stitches it is changing are outlined with its name, and a small bubble over the canvas shows what it is thinking and doing as it happens, even with the chat closed.

New tools for your model: get_brief, set_profile, read_website, capture_website, view_yarn and crop_to_yarn. list_yarn, import_yarn and import_yarn_file take reference: true for the Brief's shelf, and move_to_folder takes referenceIds.
The bundled fonts load in the desktop app on every computer. Before, they failed on any computer but the one the app was built on.
This version adds to your library, and keeps a copy of it from before. An older knitted cannot open the library after that: it says to update.

entries.title: Cards in colour, and one conversation
items: The pattern cards on a project's page show each pattern as the editor draws it, in your swatch's colours and fonts, with your pictures and parts. Before, they were grey outlines. A video's card shows it once everything in it has come in.
Knits show as a grid, each on the same card, whatever its size.

Ask is one conversation, wherever you are. The Ask page opens the chat you are having, and so does the editor's Ask panel when that chat is about the project you are in, or about the whole studio. A message sent from the editor is about the pattern open there. Both list your chats, to open another, and New chat starts a new one in both.
When your model's reply runs past the longest a reply may be, it goes on in smaller steps instead of stopping there.
The sliders in Settings, Model and Voice can be dragged. Before, they would not move. Steps per request now goes up to 100.
Your model can add a file from your computer to Yarn by its path, with import_yarn_file. It copies the file in, leaves yours as it was, and does not read hidden folders or files, such as ~/.ssh.
Your model can bring a piece of copy up to date, instead of saving another beside it, and make an empty folder ready to fill. The project's Activity shows each piece of copy it changes.
get_studio_info tells your model which knitted is answering, when that build was made and when it started, so it can tell you when an older copy is still running.
A project's Activity says in words when a part or a swatch is added, or a file is deleted from Yarn.

entries.title: Ask your model
items: Ask, in the side bar, is a conversation with your model, using your own Anthropic key from Settings, Model. Choose a project for it to work in, or the whole studio, and reply to go on: it reads the whole conversation each time. Your chats are kept, newest first.

While it works you see each step: what it reads, what it changes, and anything a lock refused. Stop ends it. Under each answer is what it changed, with a link to each pattern, and Undo all puts back every pattern that answer changed.
The editor's Ask panel is a conversation about the pattern open in it now, and each project's page has Ask your model.
Stop stops your model in the editor's Ask panel. Before, it went on to the end.

The first time 0.1.5 opens your library, it adds chats to it, after keeping a copy as it was, listed in Settings, Storage. Older versions will not open the library after that, so restore that copy to go back.

entries.title: Folders
items: Sort every section of a project into folders, and folders inside them: Patterns, Yarn, Swatch, Parts and Knits. Make one with New folder, then drag things onto it or choose Move to folder. Rename, move or delete a folder from its menu. Deleting a folder deletes nothing in it: what it held moves up a level.

Whatever you make or add goes into the folder you are in, uploads and pasted screenshots included. A search in Yarn looks in the folder you are in and every folder inside it, and says which folder each file is in.

The editor's Yarn, Parts and Patterns panels show the same folders, and the lists for choosing a file group them by folder. In Knits, Download folder makes a zip with the folders inside it kept as folders.
Your model can sort a project too, with list_folders, move_to_folder and rename, and can put what it makes straight into a folder.
The bar for the browser download no longer jumps back to the start near the end.

The first time 0.1.4 opens your library, it adds folders to it, after keeping a copy as it was, listed in Settings, Storage. Older versions will not open the library after that, so restore that copy to go back.

entries.title: Watch your model work
items: See what your model is doing while it works: its name and what it is doing, in the side bar and in the editor's top bar, with each stitch it changes outlined and named for a moment. Open it for a list of what it did and anything that was refused.
Follow takes you where your model is working and keeps up as it moves. Pause holds its changes until you resume it, and tells it to wait for you.

You and your model can edit the same pattern at once. A change of yours that lands at the same moment as its change is kept, and Undo takes back only your own. Before, the editor reloaded and your last change was lost.
The desktop app downloads the browser it knits with by itself, the first time it starts, instead of waiting for you to press Download it.
check_pattern warns when most of a picture would be cut off because its box is a very different shape, and its low-resolution warning measures the side that is stretched most.
A font in a WOFF2 file is known by its real family name, whatever the file is called, so a brand's own font is found for its swatch.

Your model can make a part from a pattern's stitches, tag Yarn as it adds it, and set the brand's corner radius when it proposes a swatch. Fonts given as {"family": ...} no longer stop a proposal, and a pattern id is enough for every pattern tool.
A model connecting over MCP is told which version of knitted it is talking to, and which tools only read.

entries.title: Knitting in the desktop app, and brands from a website
items: The desktop app downloads the browser it knits with. Before, Download it did nothing, so the app could not knit.
The download shows how far it has got, and says why if it stops. The Knit dialog offers it the first time you knit.
Adding Yarn from a link works in the desktop app, and the file keeps a readable name.

Starting a Swatch from a website finds a brand's real colours far more often: it reads the site in its own dark or light mode and takes the primary colour from its logo. You see where each colour came from and can change it before you create the Swatch, which is not used until you say so.
Your model can propose a Swatch from a website, rename its own drafts and put Yarn into image slots. check_pattern warns about a style that nothing draws.
In Yarn, a search made just after picking a kind shows what it found, not the whole library.
Arrow keys on a slider move the slider. Before, they also moved the selected stitch, when scrubbing the timeline or adjusting a style.
Settings, About shows the version you have.
The desktop app sees a new version as soon as it is out: it reads the list of releases where the installers are kept, not the website's copy.
The Download page puts the newest version first, with every older one below it.
Text on the primary button stays readable when you hover over it.

entries.title: Claude Code, pictures and updates
items: Connect Claude Code from Settings, Model. One command, and it works in knitted with the same tools and locks as the in-app model.
A project can show a picture on its card: one of its images, chosen in Projects, in Yarn, or by your model.
The desktop app updates itself. It asks once whether to check, and Check for Updates is in the menu.
The MCP page and reference list every tool, from the server's own list.

entries.title: Foundations
items: The render engine knits a Pattern frame by frame and encodes it with ffmpeg.
An MCP server lets your model list projects, read a Pattern, fill slots and knit.
Locked stitches are enforced against models. A refused write is reported back, never skipped quietly.
The design system is defined as tokens and shared by the studio and this site.
This site, the docs and the vocabulary: Pattern, Swatch, Yarn, Stitch, Knit and Part.
